chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal informed us, from his father, from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him), that he said:

Indeed, in Khurasan there is a piece of land upon which a time will come when it becomes the frequented place of the angels. A group will continuously descend from heaven while another group ascends, until the Trumpet is blown.
He was asked: O son of the Messenger of Allah, which piece of land is this? He said: It is in the land of Tus. By Allah, it is a garden from the gardens of Paradise.

Whoever visits me in that piece of land, it will be as though he visited the Messenger of Allah (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family). Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will record for him the reward of one thousand virtuous Hajj pilgrimages and one thousand accepted Umra pilgrimages, and I and my forefathers will be his intercessors on the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.الصُّورِ: the Trumpet — blown by the angel Israfil to signal the Day of Resurrection
key_terms.حَجَّةٍ مَبْرُورَةٍ: a virtuous Hajj — a pilgrimage accepted by God due to sincerity and proper conduct
key_terms.رَوْضَةٌ مِنْ رِيَاضِ الْجَنَّةِ: a garden from the gardens of Paradise — describing the sanctity of the land of Tus
key_terms.شُفَعَاؤُهُ: his intercessors — those who will plead on his behalf before God on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.مُخْتَلَفَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ: the frequented place of the angels — a place continuously visited by heavenly beings

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Rida say about the spiritual rewards of visiting his shrine in Tus, Khurasan?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) describes a sacred piece of land in Khurasan (specifically Tus, where his shrine now stands) that will become a gathering place of angels until the Day of Judgment. He declares it a garden of Paradise and promises immense spiritual rewards for visiting his resting place there, including the equivalent of a thousand Hajj and Umra pilgrimages, along with the intercession of the Imams on the Day of Resurrection. This narration was likely given to encourage the Shia community to maintain their connection to the Imam's burial site, reinforcing the theological concept of ziyarah (visitation) as a meritorious act.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Ibrahim (rh) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad al-Hamadani narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. al-Hasan b. `Ali b. Faddal informed us from his father from Abi’l Hasan `Ali b. Musa al-Rida (as). He said:

Surely, in Khurasan, there is a piece of land that will be frequented by angels at a point in time. A crowd will descend from heaven as another crowd ascends back; this will continue until the Trumpet is blown.
So, it was said to him: O son of the Messenger of Allah! Which piece of land is this? He said: It is in the land of Tus. It is, by Allah, a garden from the gardens of Paradise.

Whoever visits me in that piece of land, it will be as though he visited the Messenger of Allah (s). Allah will record the deeds of one thousand virtuous Hajj and one thousand accepted `Umra for him, and I and my forefathers will be his intercessors on the Day of Resurrection.
